title: Exceptions sampling and evidence-gathering protocol for region pins
content:
Purpose
This doc定义s a pragmatic protocol for sampling, capturing, and storing evidence when we detect region-pin exceptions (requests routed outside the requested residency boundary). The goal is to: 1) give oncall/operators consistent steps to collect minimal-for-audit artifacts, 2) produce reproducible evidence packages for legal/compliance review, and 3) enable metric-driven prioritization of fixes.

Background / motivation
- We enforce customer region pinning at the routing layer, but transient fallback (capacity/latency) and misconfiguration can cause exceptions.
- Customers and Legal ask for auditable evidence when an exception affects data residency. Current ad-hoc responses vary by engineer and leave gaps.
- This protocol focuses on sampling (not full capture) to balance privacy, cost, and forensic needs.

Scope
- Applies to hosted + dedicated routing decisions controlled by Redwood (not on-prem customer-managed stacks).
- Covers: transient fallbacks, routing-to-wrong-region errors, pin-mismatch between control-plane metadata and runtime, and operator-induced misroutes.
- Does NOT change default telemetry retention or enable continuous payload capture; only collects minimal artifacts after an incident or on-demand customer request with legal sign-off.

Principles
- Principle: minimalism. Only collect what’s required for the audit question; prefer metadata over payloads.
- Principle: reproducibility. Evidence package should contain the inputs necessary to re-run routing logic (metadata, hashes, logs), not raw user content unless legally required and approved.
- Principle: access control. Evidence packages are encrypted and access logged; stored in a compliance bucket with limited retention.
- Principle: sampling first. Capture a representative sample of affected requests rather than all requests to limit exposure and cost.

Sampling rules (operator-facing)
1) Trigger conditions (any one):
   - PagerDuty alert PIN-ROUTE-EXC or high-severity routed-exception threshold crossed (>0.05% for 5m)
   - Customer complaint escalation with suspected residency exposure
   - Ad-hoc legal/compliance request (must attach ticket id)
2) Sampling window: start at T_alert - 10m and end at T_alert + 30m by default.
3) Sampling rate:
   - Default: deterministic 1-in-100 sampling of requests that match the pin-exception predicate.
   - If customer explicitly requests full capture and Legal approves, rate can be raised to 1-in-1 for that customer for the window only.
4) Predicate for inclusion: requests where routing_decision.region != requested_region OR pin_mismatch_flag=true.
5) Priority escalation: if sampled evidence shows PII or regulated data (see detection heuristics below), escalate to Legal immediately and stop further sampling until sign-off.

What to collect (evidence package contents)
- Routing metadata (mandatory): request_id, timestamp, requested_region, routed_region, routing_policy_version, decision_trace_id, upstream_node_id, latency_ms.
- Control-plane snapshot (mandatory): customer pin config (versioned), model/version pinned, active policy rules for that tenant at time T.
- System logs (mandatory): 1-minute window of edge/router logs around the request_id, tail-sampled application logs for the involved worker. Include log lines with trace ids.
- Trace spans (recommended): distributed trace spanning API gateway -> routing -> serving runtime.
- Telemetry hashes (recommended): SHA256 of request payload (not the payload) and response payload to prove existence without storing content.
- Payload (rare, approved only): encrypted user payload/response binary (if Legal requires content-level review).
- Evidence manifest (mandatory): JSON lines list of files included, collection timestamps, collector operator id, ticket id, and short justification for capture.

Operator scripts and shortcuts (CLI snippets)
- quick-sample (recommended tool): runs automated extractor for one request_id and deposits evidence bundle to compliance bucket: 
   $ rwdctl routing sample --request REQUEST_ID --window 00:00:30 --out s3://compliance/pin-samples/PIN-421/REQUEST_ID.tar.gz
- bulk-sample (for alerts):
   $ rwdctl routing sample-batch --predicate "pin_exception=true" --start 2025-01-12T09:10Z --end 2025-01-12T09:40Z --rate 1/100 --ticket PIN-421 --out s3://compliance/pin-samples/PIN-421/
- quick-manifest view:
   $ rwdctl compliance manifest --path s3://compliance/pin-samples/PIN-421/REQUEST_ID.tar.gz
Notes: rwdctl commands call internal sampling API which enforces retentions and encryption. Only users with role 'compliance-collector' can run these commands.

Detection heuristics for PII/regulatory content (operator guidance)
- We keep lightweight detectors (regex-based + ML labelers) that run on ephemeral pipelines to flag obvious PII: SSN, credit card numbers, national id formats, and enterprise tokens.
- If a sampled request is flagged, do NOT include the raw payload in the bundle unless Legal approves. Instead include: payload hash, detector labels, and anonymized excerpts with context.

Retention, encryption, and access controls
- Evidence bundles are encrypted with KMS key kms://compliance-pin and stored in a separate S3 bucket with restricted IAM roles.
- Default retention: 90 days. Legal can request extension per-ticket for up to 2 years; extension requests must be recorded in the ticket and approved by Security.
- Access: two-person rule for decryption (requestor + approver) for bundles that include raw payloads. Metadata-only bundles can be accessed by 'compliance-audit' role with single approver.

Audit package checklist (what to attach to ticket)
- Incident ticket id (PIN-421) and summary of trigger.
- Evidence bundle path + manifest.
- Short explanation of root cause hypothesis (routing config change, autoscaler fallback, zone outage, etc.).
- Whether raw payloads were included and Legal sign-off id.
- Suggested immediate mitigations (pin-enforcement toggle, route hold, model pin rollback).

Playbook: step-by-step (first 30 minutes)
1) Triage: confirm alert, add ticket PIN-xxx, set priority. Snapshot current control-plane config (one command).
2) Run quick bulk-sample for the alert window at default 1/100. Upload bundle to compliance bucket.
3) Review manifest and hashes while running root-cause checks (control-plane history, recent deploys, infra incidents).
4) If evidence suggests more than transient exposure (>=5 sampled exceptions or one exception with PII), pause sampling and call Legal; follow two-person rule for any content-level capture.
5) Post initial triage, communicate templated customer note (see /templates/customer-pin-exposure.md) and internal exec summary.

Open questions / TODOs\- Need product decision: should the default sampling rate be higher for enterprise tiers? (tag: product-decision)\- Improve detector false positive rate: assign ML ticket to applied-ml for precision tuning (jira: PIN-ML-12).\- Instrument automated detection that surfaces likely root cause (config drift vs infra fallback).\- Add unit tests & e2e for rwdctl sample commands in CI.

References
- Confluence: Residency enforcement design (linked above)
- Jira: PIN-421 (investigation), PIN-ML-12 (detector improvements)
- Github PR: region-routing/PR/177 (recent routing policy change)

Appendix: Example evidence manifest (example lines)
- manifest.jsonl:
  {"file":"routing_metadata.json","sha256":"abc123...","collected_at":"2025-01-12T09:16:12Z"}
  {"file":"control_plane_config.json","sha256":"def456...","collected_at":"2025-01-12T09:16:25Z"}
  {"file":"edge_logs_09-10_09-40.gz","sha256":"789fed...","collected_at":"2025-01-12T09:17:01Z"}

Notes to operators (quick reminders)
- Don’t ever move raw customer payloads into an unsecured location — default tools block this but double-check.
- If Legal asks for content, require ticket id and the two-person approver names in the ticket before running a payload capture.
- When in doubt, sample metadata and escalate; metadata is usually enough for routing audits.

Last updated: 2025-11-21 (Claire Nguyen)
